stories.title: University of Ottawa
stories.imageAlt: Placeholder card for University of Ottawa research experience
stories.content: Tested open-source deep-learning models that predict spatial gene expression from histology images.
stories.popupContent: I worked with an Assistant Professor of Biotechnology at the University of Ottawa to evaluate deep-learning models that predict spatial gene expression from images of tissue slices. Using Google Colab, I ran inference on professor-provided sample data and analyzed the resulting gene-expression predictions. I tested a range of open-source approaches, including models based on transformers, graph neural networks, contrastive learning, and image-to-RNA translation. Their outputs were compared with results from models developed in-house by the research team. Representative models that can be named publicly include Hist2ST, BLEEP, THItoGene, and HE2Gene.

stories.title: Sharkbyte
stories.description: Web Development Co-op Student - February 2024 - June 2024
stories.content: Helped build the customer-facing interface of a full-stack e-commerce prototype after completing an intensive three-week introduction to web development.
stories.popupContent: During my high-school co-op at Sharkbyte, I worked with approximately 30 students to build a full-stack e-commerce prototype. The team was divided between frontend and backend development, with separate groups working on the customer and administrator interfaces. I contributed to the customer-facing side of the website, primarily working on the homepage, search interface, and product pages. We first designed pages collaboratively in Figma and then recreated the designs using HTML, CSS, PHP, and Tailwind CSS, with SQL supporting the website's database. One of the biggest challenges was closely matching the Figma designs using Tailwind CSS while learning how interface design, frontend code, backend functionality, databases, and basic web security fit together.

stories.title: CellChem Pharmaceuticals
stories.description: Graphic Design & Web Support Intern - June 2024 - July 2024
stories.imageAlt: Placeholder card for CellChem Pharmaceuticals experience
stories.content: Redesigned pharmaceutical packaging content and created website-interface mockups during a one-month placement.
stories.popupContent: During my placement at CellChem Pharmaceuticals, I supported the design of packaging for imported medicines being prepared for approval and sale in the Canadian market. Some existing packaging needed clearer text and informational tables, so I used Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop to revise text layouts, improve readability, and update graphics. I also reviewed parts of the company website, identified interface problems, and created mockups showing how pages such as the medicine slideshow and downloadable product list could be presented more clearly. I worked directly with the company's designer, presented completed versions, incorporated requested revisions, and supplied the updated design files. Because the placement lasted only one month, I do not know whether the packaging designs were ultimately manufactured or adopted.
